names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Νοεμβρίου, «Όσιος Γεννάδιος ο Βατοπαιδινός», with the rank words left off. The epithet «ο Βατοπαιδινός» is left to the display name; he is not the patriarch Gennadius kept in another line of the same day.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 17. новембар ст. ст., „Преп. Генадије Ватопедски.“ — «Преп.» is the `venerable` grade `types` already keeps and comes off. «Ватопедски» is the monastery he belonged to: not a rank and not a see, and this folder carries no `office` for it, so §6's rule that the form keeps everything which distinguishes him keeps it. THIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE READING THE GREEK FORM ON THIS FOLDER TOOK, which left «ο Βατοπαιδινός» to the display name — and the difference is the point: a bare «Генадије» would fold onto `gennadius-patriarch-of-constantinople`, whom the same calendars keep elsewhere and whom this folder's own Greek note is at pains to say he is not. Measured: no other folder holds this two-word string.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Νοεμβρίου — «Όσιος Γεννάδιος ο Βατοπαιδινός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole notice is three sentences: he was **δοχειάρης** of the monastery of Vatopedi on the Holy Mountain — the page glosses the word itself, the monk responsible for filling the monastery's vessels with oil — he was counted worthy to see an empty jar well up with oil by a miracle of the Mother of God, and he died in peace. **He is not the patriarch Gennadius** whom the same day keeps in another line, and the two are deliberately kept apart: one is a fifth-century patriarch of Constantinople with a folder already, the other an Athonite cellarer, and the page gives them separate entries. **No `dates`, no `locations`, no `related` and no hymn**: the page gives none of them, and does not say in whose time the miracle happened. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.11.2025 (17. новембар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Генадије Ватопедски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, three sentences, and the same three saint.gr prints: the office, the oil and the attribution of the wonder to the Mother of God. STILL NO `dates`: this book gives him no century, no abbot and no reign either, so the folder's `dates` stays null, which is what two sources now agree in withholding. No `related`: the entry names no person. WHAT IT ADDS to what the folder had: that the vessel was an EMPTIED CASK rather than a jar, and that the miracle was ascribed not only to the Most Holy Theotokos, to whom the monastery is dedicated, but PARTICULARLY TO AN ICON OF HERS THAT STOOD THERE — the icon is not named and no feast of it is claimed here.
